keyQuotes: The 2026 World Cup is destined to be an extremely precise, extremely commercialized, and extremely realistic tournament.

Can the old lion kings, before being brought down by the modern wolves, shatter the machine with an unreasonable through ball or long-range strike? This is the biggest romantic suspense of this World Cup.
Football is not a science. Football has more unpredictability than basketball or volleyball. This is precisely what makes football so captivating.
The World Cup will witness many suns we have long awaited reaching their zenith, and even more stars you have never known will shine brightly.

mainPoints.explanation: The expansion to 48 teams and 104 matches extends the schedule to maximize traffic monetization; the convergence of global youth training leads to tactical modularity, with high pressing and space utilization becoming a universal language, reducing the number of surprise teams.
mainPoints.point: The 2026 World Cup will be highly industrialized and commercialized.

mainPoints.explanation: Short videos, tactical GIFs, and data charts break the game into countless clips. Fans no longer sit around to watch the entire match but consume and discuss it in real-time, turning the World Cup into a massive, fluid spectacle.
mainPoints.point: Media dissemination shifts from complete narratives to fragmented flows.

mainPoints.explanation: Legends like Messi, Ronaldo, and Modrić will play in their final World Cup, while new generations like Mbappé, Kane, and Yamal aim for the title. Whether the veterans' moments of brilliance can shatter the industrial machine is the greatest romantic suspense.
mainPoints.point: The farewell of veterans and the rise of the new generation form the biggest suspense of this tournament.

mainPoints.explanation: No matter the pre-tournament predictions, the World Cup always produces surprises and new legends. This ability to defy expectations is its most captivating core and a trait that distinguishes football from other sports.
mainPoints.point: The eternal charm of the World Cup lies in its unpredictable nature.

oneSentenceSummary: Using the 1994 World Cup as a reference, this article looks ahead to the 2026 World Cup from the perspectives of expanded format, media dissemination, tactical convergence, and generational shifts, anticipating its industrialized and commercialized characteristics while retaining a romantic expectation for football's unpredictability and legendary narratives.
originalTitle: 2026 年世界杯？到底会是什么样？
summary: The article uses the 1994 World Cup in the United States as a historical anchor to compare and forecast the 2026 World Cup. The author points out that the 2026 World Cup will be highly industrialized and commercialized: the expansion to 48 teams and 104 matches aims to reach more people and monetize traffic; the convergence of global youth training leads to tactical modularity, with high pressing and space utilization becoming a universal language; short videos and streaming services break the game into fragmented content, replacing traditional complete narratives. At the same time, the article also focuses on the final World Cup for veterans like Messi and Ronaldo, as well as the impact of new generations like Mbappé and Kane. The author argues that despite the increasing precision of the football industry, the World Cup's unpredictability and myth-making ability—those unexpected upsets and legends—remain its most captivating core. The article concludes by recalling the viewing experience of each World Cup from a fan's perspective, emphasizing that the charm of the World Cup lies in the fact that it never follows a preset script.
title: The 2026 World Cup? What Will It Really Be Like?
